report_name: US Seizes Hacking Tools Used by China-Linked Group Flax Typhoon

threat_actors.name: Flax Typhoon
threat_actors.description: A sophisticated Chinese state-sponsored threat actor focused on intelligence gathering and initial access operations. This campaign involved the use of custom tools, Microscan and FishHub, to target critical infrastructure, government, and educational institutions in the U.S., Taiwan, and other allied nations.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering and initial access to sensitive political, economic, and military information.

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Flax Typhoon used the Microscan tool, operated via a Mirai botnet, to conduct widespread vulnerability scanning against critical sectors to identify potential targets.

attack_patterns.name: Develop Capabilities
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor group developed and operated custom hacking tools, Microscan and FishHub, to support their campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure
attack_patterns.description: Flax Typhoon acquired infrastructure, including seven command and control domains and a botnet of Mirai-infected IoT devices, to support their operations.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: The FishHub platform was utilized to conduct targeted spearphishing campaigns to deliver malicious payloads and gain initial access to victim networks.

attack_patterns.name: External Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: Flax Typhoon deployed SoftEther VPN software on compromised systems to maintain long-term, encrypted access to victim networks for persistence.

malware.name: Microscan
malware.description: A custom hacking tool developed by Integrity Technology Group and used by Flax Typhoon for large-scale vulnerability scanning. It was operated via a Mirai botnet to obfuscate its origin.

malware.name: FishHub
malware.description: A custom spearphishing platform developed by Integrity Technology Group and used by Flax Typhoon to deliver malicious payloads and gain initial access to targeted networks.

malware.name: Mirai
malware.description: A botnet of Mirai-infected IoT devices was used to operate the Microscan vulnerability scanning tool, obfuscating the origin of the scanning activity.

tools.name: SoftEther VPN
tools.description: Legitimate VPN software deployed by Flax Typhoon on compromised systems to establish persistent, encrypted remote access for long-term espionage and data theft.

vulnerabilities.name: Flax Typhoon Exploited Vulnerabilities (CISA KEV)
vulnerabilities.description: A group of five unnamed CVEs exploited by Flax Typhoon for initial access, which were added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog as part of the disruption announcement.

identities.name: U.S. Department of Justice
identities.description: U.S. government agency that, along with the FBI, conducted a court-authorized operation to seize and disrupt infrastructure used by Flax Typhoon.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation
identities.description: U.S. law enforcement agency that, along with the DOJ, seized hacking tools and domains linked to Flax Typhoon.

identities.name: Integrity Technology Group
identities.description: A Chinese company sanctioned by the U.S. for developing the Microscan and FishHub hacking tools used by Flax Typhoon.

identities.name: U.S. Critical Infrastructure
identities.description: A class of victims in the United States targeted by Flax Typhoon's scanning and compromise activities.

identities.name: Taiwanese Government and University Targets
identities.description: A class of victims in Taiwan targeted by Flax Typhoon's FishHub spearphishing platform, including at least 20 universities.

identities.name: Japanese and Polish Airports
identities.description: A class of critical infrastructure victims in Japan and Poland targeted by Flax Typhoon.

identities.name: South Carolina Power Company
identities.description: A power company in South Carolina, US, that was targeted by Flax Typhoon's Microscan tool.

infrastructure.name: Flax Typhoon C2 Domains
infrastructure.description: Seven domains used for command and control of the Microscan and FishHub tools, which were seized by the DOJ and FBI.

infrastructure.name: Mirai Botnet for Scanning
infrastructure.description: A botnet of Mirai-infected IoT devices used by Flax Typhoon to operate the Microscan tool and obfuscate the origin of their vulnerability scanning.
